datasets.name: Curated black-hole catalogue (13 objects) with per-value references
datasets.organization: Published literature (Gaia Collaboration, LIGO/Virgo, EHT, X-ray binary and AGN dynamical-mass papers); curated by the Cosmos project
datasets.purpose: Stellar and supermassive black holes shown in the exhibit: position, distance, mass, spin, companion, orbit, jet and discovery data
datasets.mechanism: Hand-curated from the cited papers (arXiv abstracts or full text) into JSON; no network access at runtime; validated by scripts/data/blackholes/build-doc.mjs
datasets.version: schemaVersion 1; generated 2026-10-20; every value cites an entry of the file's own references table (42 references, e.g. El-Badry et al. 2023, Gaia Collaboration Panuzzo et al. 2024, Miller-Jones et al. 2021)
datasets.license: Factual measurements transcribed from published papers (facts are not copyrightable); no third-party text or images are redistributed. Individual papers keep their own licences. Not recorded: per-paper licence terms.
datasets.citation: See the 'references' object in blackholes.json for the full per-value list, each with citation and URL (e.g. Gaia Collaboration, Panuzzo et al. 2024, A&A 686, L2; Miller-Jones et al. 2021, Science 371, 1046; Reid et al. 2014, ApJ 796, 2; Gaia Collaboration, Vallenari et al. 2023, A&A 674, A1).
datasets.rateLimits: n/a (no network access; static transcription from papers)
datasets.updateCadence: manual; revisit when new dynamical-mass or Gaia astrometric results are published
datasets.normalization: Hand curation; scripts/data/blackholes/build-doc.mjs checks that every value has a resolvable reference and regenerates docs/data/blackholes.md. Quoted errors are 1-sigma unless a field note says otherwise (GW150914 90% credible; Greene et al. 2001 95%); null means unknown or not verified, never zero; coordinates are ICRS decimal degrees; a few values marked 'derived' in notes were computed from published quantities (companion mass = q x M_BH, distance = 1/parallax).
datasets.fallback: Black holes whose entry is missing are not drawn; positions flagged positionIllustrative are placed for display only.
datasets.limitations: Curated by hand, so transcription errors are possible. Many masses are model-dependent (inclination, mass-ratio assumptions) and carry wide errors. Entries with positionIllustrative true are not measured positions. Some values are derived from published quantities rather than quoted directly.

datasets.name: Event Horizon Telescope 2019 image of M87*
datasets.organization: Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration (images published by ESO under CC BY 4.0)
datasets.purpose: The real 1.3 mm radio image of the M87* shadow, shown beside the rendered black hole in the approach readout
datasets.mechanism: Single JPEG committed to the repository and displayed by src/domains/blackholes/readout.ts; the download URL and any resizing were not recorded in the repo
datasets.version: EHT 2019 M87* image (EHT Collaboration 2019, ApJL 875, L1)
datasets.license: CC BY 4.0 (EHT Collaboration, as credited in the in-app caption; the repo notes the image as CC BY 4.0). Credit EHT Collaboration.
datasets.citation: The Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration 2019, ApJL 875, L1, 'First M87 Event Horizon Telescope Results. I. The Shadow of the Supermassive Black Hole'. In-app caption: 'The real M87*: Event Horizon Telescope 2019, 1.3 mm radio. EHT Collaboration, CC BY 4.0.'
datasets.normalization: None recorded beyond JPEG storage (file mtime 2026-10-20 16:23 local; used as the retrieval time).
datasets.fallback: The real-image thumbnail is omitted from the readout and the rendered black hole is shown alone.
datasets.limitations: A reconstructed interferometric radio image (1.3 mm), not a photograph, representing one epoch only. Original download URL and processing are not recorded.
